analyses.description: This table contains mineral abundances and analytical errors derived from diffraction-all K-alpha diffraction data for the Marimba2 drill sample, analyzed in CheMin cell number 8b (Mylar window). This is a P2 revision of the original MIN file that was created on 2017-02-14T15:26:15. The P2 reanalysis recognizes that olivine is not present in Marimba2, based on absence of the strongest olivine diffraction peak. Analysis is based on RDA file CMB_524082694RDA14260561236CH00113P1. That RDA file is from the first night of analysis, sol 1425-1426. Additional analyses of Marimba2 were obtained on subsequent nights, but warm temperatures inside CheMin (up to ~30 degrees centigrade, with correspondingly low relative humidity) caused conversion of gypsum to bassanite over time. Therefore these later analyses do not represent in situ mineralogy and are not used to determine the RDA diffraction pattern and MIN composition of the in situ sample. For comparison, the full RDA file for all four nights of analysis, which is not used to prepare a MIN file, is CMB_524082694RDA14260561236CH00113P2. Mineral identifications, abundances and analytical errors for crystalline phases, other than clay minerals, were determined using the program JADE. Orthorhombic and monoclinic pyroxenes both appear to be present, with orthopyroxene predominant, but exact identification of individual pyroxenes is hampered by small abundances and only the percentage of total pyroxene is reported. In addition to the crystalline phases, the abundance of clay minerals was modeled using the program FULLPAT at ~23 +/- 12 weight% of the total sample. A broad rise in background is present and has been modeled using FULLPAT to indicate that ~40 +/- 20 weight% of the total sample consists of X-ray amorphous material. Errors quoted are 2-sigma. Column 1 of the table lists mineral identifications, column 2 lists the mineral abundances in weight percent. Errors shown in column 3 are 2-sigma and include the combined instrumental error plus analytical error estimated from five separate JADE analyses by members of the CheMin team. In Marimba2 the combined errors in pyroxene abundance produce a 1-sigma error comparable to the estimated abundance, but analysis of the full four nights of Marimba2 data in CMB_524082694RDA14260561236CH00113P2 confirms that pyroxene is present.
